Subject: Post-call: performance SLOs & VPC qualification (ACME)

Hi Tom / Lina —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + agreed next steps on the performance and networking items so we stay aligned: 

Summary of ACME requirements (as discussed):
- 95th p95 latency target for streaming responses: <= 120 ms (end-to-end for your front-end -> model stream).
- Sustained throughput: 250 concurrent streaming connections (concurrency = active open streams delivering tokens).
- Token generation rate: ~30 tokens/sec per stream average; burst up to 80 tokens/sec in short windows.
- Persistence: KV cache warmups expected per session; cold-start behavior acceptable within 300 ms extra.

Network / deployment constraints:
- Private deployment in your VPC (we discussed VPC peering or VPN).
- Egress policy: all inference egress must stay within ACME-managed VPCs; no public egress for payloads containing PII.
- Internal latency budget from ACME app -> Redwood private endpoint: target 30-50 ms one-way.

Agreed next steps:
1) ACME: share traceroute/mtr from your app infra to the candidate subnet we provided (we need path & hop counts).
2) ACME: confirm whether you prefer VPN peering or AWS VPC Peering (we recommended peering for lowest latency).
3) Redwood: provide a compact SLO matrix & recommended kernel/quantization profile for the estimated workload (Jordan will send).
4) Both: schedule a short network debug session (30 min) to validate MTU, firewall rules, and NAT egress behavior.

Please reply here with the traceroute + preferred peering option; we can kick off the network session as soon as tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Tom / Lina —

Attaching a compact SLO matrix and checklist. Key engineering notes:
- Recommendation: AWS VPC Peering into a dedicated private subnet in us-west-2. Peering gives ~8-15 ms median one-way compared to VPN’s 20-40 ms typical.
- MTU: Ensure 1500 across the path; fragmentation increases latency on large payloads.
- TCP keepalives: set to 60s on your side; Redwood will keep session heartbeats every 45s to prevent idle timeouts.
- NAT Gateways: if egress to the public internet is possible from the host subnet, prefer a NAT with 10k+ ephemeral ports or use EIPs assigned per host pool to avoid port exhaustion during high concurrency.
- Streaming concurrency: we recommend a per-node config of 60 concurrent streams when using our optimized kernel; you can scale horizontally.
- Cold-starts: KV cache warm-starts typically add 150-300 ms; recommend warmup for critical endpoints or pre-warmed pools.

Attachments: network-diagram.png, redwood-slo-matrix.pdf

If possible, please run these from one of your app hosts (replace <host-ip> below):
- traceroute -n <redwood-subnet-ip>
- curl -v --http2 https://<redwood-endpoint>/health

I can join the network debug session with our infra engineer (Rishi) if you want deeper packet captures.

-Jordan
